title: Dataset tiers and freeze timeline
author: Faye Niu
purpose: Show which D0 and separately authorised D1 evidence may inform one versioned evaluation freeze, preserve D2 as an untouched company-period out-of-sample holdout until approved access, and bound subsequent C0-C3 execution, adjudication and analysis without inventing a fourth dataset tier or a confirmatory result.

status.interpretation: A methodology, access and evidence-class boundary. The current manifest states are repository facts; no pilot, holdout, manual, participant or final comparative outcome is asserted.

limitations: The exhibit is conceptual author synthesis and does not report an empirical result.
It contains no sample size, participant count, prevalence, accuracy, effect size, confidence interval, threshold, time, token, cost, coverage, usability or human-benefit value.
The figure does not imply that D1 or D2 has been executed, that D2 has been opened, or that final C0-C3 evaluation has occurred.
D0 synthetic mechanism and regression evidence cannot be generalised to real portfolio, practitioner, participant, production or investment outcomes.

Visible D0 state, namespace, classification and partition-policy wording describes declarations in fixtures/evaluation_manifest.json; the exhibit does not independently demonstrate loader enforcement, namespace rewriting or group-partition isolation.
D1 may inform a freeze only after separate authority and must retain pilot or exploratory labelling as specified by the protocol.
Freezing, manifesting and sealing reduce leakage risk but do not guarantee reference truth, correct adjudication, protocol validity, representativeness, reproducibility or external validity.
The current C0 and participant-based C3 states remain held; synthetic D0 measurements cannot substitute for their unavailable outcomes.
Participant observations are part of authorised workflow-condition execution, not an additional dataset tier.
The PDF is vector-only but is not claimed to be tagged; the complete TXT alternative provides a linear accessible companion.
